## fleet

> Short/medium-haul single-aisle utilisation of ~10–11 block hours and ~4 cycles a day is typical of hub-and-spoke operations (order-of-magnitude, not operator data).

> Long-haul twin-aisle aircraft fly more hours and far fewer cycles per day.

> Summer (Jul–Aug) and year-end holiday peaks are typical for a Gulf hub; factors are illustrative.

> Grounding does not reduce scheduled exposure (protection via spare aircraft / sub-charter assumed). Lost flying is costed through the AOG penalty. Keeps exogenous demand identical across policies for paired comparison.

## engine

> Shop capacity slots are interpreted as bench/test-stand positions: a unit holds a slot only for its touch/test time (share of work time); awaiting-parts and paperwork time runs outside the slot. Without this, 14 slots could not process ~1,500 rotable removals a year at 15–90 day TATs.
